subject: Follow-up: Observability & PII constraints — pulsehealth discovery
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Turner <lisa@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: Observability & PII constraints — pulsehealth discovery

Hi Lisa — thanks again for the 30-minute call earlier. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so nothing gets lost in follow-ups. I tried to keep this concise.

Call summary (what we heard)
- Primary pain: need low-latency inference for patient-facing triage workflows while ensuring PHI never persists in readable logs or third-party telemetry.
- Current stack: in-house microservices + a small fleet of GPUs running an open model; logging via Splunk; identity via Okta.
- Constraints called out:
  - No raw PHI in any vendor-hosted logs; audit trails must show request/response metadata without storing sensitive fields.
  - Field-level redaction required (names, MRNs, SSNs) prior to any long-term retention or analytics.
  - Retention split: short-lived request traces (30 days) vs. aggregated metrics (indefinite/rolling).
  - Technical must-haves: exportable audit logs (machine-readable), BYOK for keys, and SOC 2 + penetration test evidence.

Success criteria we discussed (what would make this a successful pilot)
- PHI protection: demonstrable redaction layer with configurable field rules and no plaintext PHI written to durable logs.
- Traceability: per-request audit record (id, timestamp, model version, route) exportable to your SIEM.
- Latency: 95th percentile <250ms for the triage endpoint under expected sample load (we'll baseline with your perf tests).
- Cost/ops: predictable unit costs; ability to run in a dedicated or private deployment if required.

Risks/unknowns we flagged
- How much pre-processing you want us to take on vs. doing redaction client-side.
- Exact retention policy mapping for different data classes.

Attachments shared with this email
- redwood-data-protection-checklist.pdf (high-level mapping of controls + optional deployment modes)
- pulsehealth-ma-poc-scope.xlsx (blank scope template for pilot sizing)

Proposed next steps
1) I’ll share SOC2 + pen test summary and a short whitepaper on our redaction approach by EOW (attachment + link).
2) Please share a short IOC doc: example payloads (sanitized) and which fields must be redacted vs. aggregated (Monica can take a look).
3) If okay, we’ll propose two pilot options: Dedicated Reserved Pool (predictable throughput) and Private (VPC/BYOK) with cost estimates; Aditya will scope pricing.
4) Schedule a brief tech follow-up (30 min) with your infra/security folks to align on BYOK and audit log formats.

Would Tuesday or Wednesday next week work for the tech follow-up?

Thanks again — appreciate Lisa and the security team's time.

— Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182
Redwood Inference

From: Lisa Turner <lisa@pulsehealth.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: PulseHealth Security <security@pulsehealth.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Observability & PII constraints — pulsehealth discovery

Hi Dylan — thanks for the clear summary, that matches our notes. A few clarifications and adds from security: 

- Field-level redaction: important — we want the vendor to support both client-side redaction SDKs and server-side rules. For the pilot we plan to do client-side redaction of direct identifiers (names, MRNs) and ask Redwood to demonstrate server-side redaction for derived PII.
- Retention: we need a default of 30 days for request-level traces. Aggregated metrics (non-PII) can be kept longer for product analytics. If you offer Private with BYOK, we'd keep traces even shorter (7–14 days) if you can guarantee cryptographic separation.
- Audit logs: must be exportable to our Splunk collector in JSONL; each log line should include an immutable request_id, timestamp, model_version, and route.
- Compliance materials: please include SOC 2 type II report, recent pen test summary, and your standard DPA draft.

For next steps — Tuesday 2027-02-23 at 10am PT works for the tech follow-up (I’ll invite our infra and security leads). For the pricing, could you give a ballpark for dedicated vs private for a pilot sized for ~1k daily requests (with spiky peaks)? We just need order-of-magnitude to decide whether to pursue dedicated or private.

Thanks — Lisa
Lisa Turner
Director, Product & Security
PulseHealth
lisa@pulsehealth.com | +1 212-555-0199
